page.name: Tenant isolation
page.h1: One tenant per account, one set of credentials each
page.metaDescription: Connections, API keys and message records are held per tenant, so one account’s credentials and traffic are never another’s.
page.lede: Isolation is the feature that nobody asks about until it is missing. Holding connections, keys and records per tenant means a shared platform does not become a shared inbox.

sections.h: What is scoped to a tenant

p: A tenant boundary is also a blast radius boundary: a compromised key sends from one tenant’s accounts rather than everyone’s, and usage reported for one account is measured from that account’s own traffic.

Isolation is a structural boundary in how credentials and records are held. It sits alongside your own access control rather than replacing it, and the obligations that follow from your data stay on your side.

faq.q: Can two teams share one tenant?
faq.a: A tenant is the unit that holds connections and keys. Whether two teams share one or have separate tenants is a decision about your own access model.

faq.q: Are message logs visible across tenants?
faq.a: Records are held per tenant; a tenant sees its own sends, not another’s.
